questions.question: If an IP network uses a subnet mask of [latex]255.255.240.0[/latex], the maximum number of IP addresses that can be assigned to network interfaces is ________. (answer in integer)
questions.explanation:
Subnet mask [latex]255.255.240.0[/latex] in binary: [latex]11111111.11111111.11110000.00000000[/latex] — this has [latex]20[/latex] network bits (a [latex]/20[/latex]).

Host bits [latex]=32-20=12[/latex], giving [latex]2^{12}=4096[/latex] total addresses in the subnet. Of these, [latex]2[/latex] are reserved (the all-zeros network address and the all-ones broadcast address) and cannot be assigned to interfaces.

Usable addresses [latex]=4096-2=4094[/latex].

Answer: 4094

questions.question: Which one of the following protocols may need to broadcast some of its messages?
questions.explanation:
DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) is used by a host to automatically obtain an IP address (and other network configuration) when it first joins a network — since the host doesn't yet have an IP address (or know the server's address), its initial "DHCP Discover" message must be broadcast on the local network so that any DHCP server present can respond.

[latex]\text{SMTP}[/latex] (mail), [latex]\text{FTP}[/latex] (file transfer), and [latex]\text{HTTP}[/latex] (web) are all conventional client-server protocols that communicate with a specific, already-known server address over a normal unicast connection — they have no inherent need to broadcast.

Answer: DHCP

questions.question:
A machine receives an IPv4 datagram. The protocol field of the IPv4 header has the protocol number of a protocol X.
Which ONE of the following is NOT a possible candidate for X?
questions.explanation:
The IPv4 protocol field identifies which higher-layer protocol's data the datagram carries, using standard registered numbers: ICMP [latex]=1[/latex], IGMP [latex]=2[/latex], OSPF [latex]=89[/latex] — all of these run directly over IP and have their own dedicated protocol number.

RIP, however, is not carried directly over IP; it runs as an application-layer protocol on top of UDP (using UDP port [latex]520[/latex]). So an IP datagram carrying RIP traffic would have its protocol field set to UDP's number ([latex]17[/latex]), never a dedicated "RIP" protocol number.

Answer: Routing Information Protocol (RIP)

questions.question:
It is necessary to design a link-layer protocol between two hosts that are directly connected over a lossless link of length [latex]3000[/latex] kilometers. Assume that the link bandwidth is [latex]10^8[/latex] bits per second and that the propagation delay in the link is [latex]5[/latex] nanoseconds per meter. Every transmitted data byte is assigned a unique sequence number.

Let [latex]N[/latex] be the minimum number of bits needed for the sequence number field in the protocol header such that:

(i) the sequence numbers do not wrap around before [latex]60[/latex] seconds, and
(ii) the maximum utilization of the link is achieved.

The value of [latex]N[/latex] is ______. (answer in integer)
questions.explanation:
Propagation delay (one-way) [latex]=3000\text{ km}\times5\text{ ns/m}=3{,}000{,}000\text{ m}\times5\text{ ns}=15{,}000{,}000\text{ ns}=15[/latex] ms, so round-trip time [latex]\text{RTT}=30[/latex] ms [latex]=0.03[/latex] s.

Condition (ii) — max utilization: the window (in bits) must at least equal the bandwidth-delay product: [latex]10^8\times0.03=3\times10^6[/latex] bits [latex]=375{,}000[/latex] bytes, requiring at least [latex]\lceil\log_2(375000)\rceil\approx19[/latex] sequence-number bits.

Condition (i) — no wraparound within 60 s: total bytes sent in [latex]60[/latex] s at full bandwidth [latex]=\dfrac{10^8\times60}{8}=750{,}000{,}000[/latex] bytes, requiring [latex]2^N\ge750{,}000{,}000[/latex], i.e. [latex]N\ge\lceil\log_2(750{,}000{,}000)\rceil=30[/latex] (since [latex]2^{29}\approx5.37\times10^8<7.5\times10^8\le2^{30}\approx1.07\times10^9[/latex]).

Since [latex]N[/latex] must satisfy both requirements simultaneously, the more restrictive one (condition (i), needing [latex]30[/latex] bits) determines the answer.

Answer: 30

The propagation speed of the media is 4x[latex]10^{6}[/latex] meters per second. It is needed to design a Go-Back-N sliding window protocol for this network. The average packet size is [latex]10^{7}[/latex] bits. The network is to be used to its full capacity. Assume that processing delays at nodes are negligible. Then, the minimum size in bits of the sequence number field has to be ___________.

Checking each statement:
- [latex]T_p=\frac{8\times10^6}{4\times10^6}=2[/latex] s
- [latex]T_t=\frac{10^7}{5\times10^8}=0.02[/latex] s

Window for full use = [latex]1+\frac{2T_p}{T_t}=1+200=201[/latex]. Go-Back-N needs at least W + 1 = 202 sequence numbers.

[latex]2^8=256\ge202[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 8 bits

Answer: 8

questions.question:
A TCP server application is programmed to listen on port number P on host S. A TCP client is connected to the TCP server over the network.
Consider that while the TCP connection was active, the server machine S crashed and rebooted. Assume that the client does not use the TCP keepalive timer. Which of the following behaviors is/are possible?

options.A: If the client was waiting to receive a packet, it may wait indefinitely.
options.B: The TCP server application on S can listen on P after reboot.
options.C: If the client sends a packet after the server reboot, it will receive a RST segment.
options.D: If the client sends a packet after the server reboot, it will receive a FIN segment.

questions.explanation:
Checking each statement:
- The client gets no notice of the crash; without keepalive, a client waiting to receive may wait forever [latex]\text{---}[/latex] possible.
- After reboot the application can bind and listen on port P again [latex]\text{---}[/latex] possible.
- The rebooted server has no record of the old connection, so a segment from the client gets a RST [latex]\text{---}[/latex] possible.
- FIN is sent only on a normal close of a known connection [latex]\text{---}[/latex] not possible.

Answer: Options 1, 2 and 3

questions.question:
Consider a simple communication system where multiple nodes are connected by a shared broadcast medium (like Ethernet or wireless). The nodes in the system use the following carrier-sense based medium access protocol. A node that receives a packet to transmit will carrier-sense the medium for 5 units of time. If the node does not detect any other transmission in this duration, it starts transmitting its packet in the next time unit. If the node detects another transmission, it waits until this other transmission finishes, and then begins to carrier-sense for 5 time units again. Once they start to transmit, nodes do not perform any collision detection and continue transmission even if a collision occurs. All transmissions last for 20 units of time. Assume that the transmission signal travels at the speed of 10 meters per unit time in the medium.
Assume that the system has two nodes P and Q, located at a distance d meters from each other. P starts transmitting a packet at time t=0 after successfully completing its carrier-sense phase. Node Q has a packet to transmit at time t=0 and begins to carrier-sense the medium.
The maximum distance d (in meters, rounded to the closest integer) that allows Q to successfully avoid a collision between its proposed transmission and P's ongoing transmission is _____.
questions.explanation:
Q senses from t = 0 to t = 5 and would start at t = 6. To avoid a collision, Q must notice P's signal while sensing, i.e. it must arrive by t = 5:
[latex]\frac{d}{10}\le5\Rightarrow d\le50[/latex] m

Answer: 50

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.question: Consider sending an IP datagram of size 1420 bytes (including 20 bytes of IP header) from a sender to a receiver over a path of two links with a router between them. The first link (sender to router) has an MTU (Maximum Transmission Unit) size of 542 bytes, while the second link (router to receiver) has an MTU size of 360 bytes. The number of fragments that would be delivered at the receiver is _____
questions.explanation:
Data in datagram [latex]=1420-20=1400[/latex] bytes. Fragment data (except the last) must be a multiple of 8.

Link 1 (MTU 542): max data [latex]=522[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] use 520. Fragments: 520, 520, 360.
Link 2 (MTU 360): max data [latex]=340[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] use 336.
- 520 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 336 + 184
- 520 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 336 + 184
- 360 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 336 + 24

Fragments are reassembled only at the receiver, so it receives [latex]2+2+2=6[/latex] fragments.

Answer: 6

questions.question: Assume that the bandwidth for a TCP connection is 1048560 bits/sec. Let [latex]\alpha[/latex] be the value of RTT in milliseconds (rounded off to the nearest integer) after which the TCP window scale option is needed. Let [latex]\beta[/latex] be the maximum possible window size with window scale option. Then the values of [latex]\alpha[/latex] and [latex]\beta[/latex] are
questions.explanation:

Scaling is needed once bandwidth [latex]\times[/latex] RTT exceeds 65535: RTT = 65535 / 131070 = 0.5 s = 500 ms.

The max scale shift is 14, so [latex]\beta=65535\times2^{14}[/latex].

Answer: 500 milliseconds, 65535 [latex]\times[/latex] [latex]2^{14}[/latex]

questions.question: Consider a TCP connection between a client and a server with the following specifications; the round trip time is 6 ms, the size of the receiver advertised window is 50 KB, slow-start threshold at the client is 32 KB, and the maximum segment size is 2 KB. The connection is established at time t=0. Assume that there are no timeouts and errors during transmission. Then the size of the congestion window (in KB) at time t+60 ms after all acknowledgements are processed is _______
questions.explanation:
cwnd starts at 1 MSS = 2 KB and doubles every RTT (6 ms) in slow start, up to ssthresh = 32 KB. After that it grows by 1 MSS = 2 KB per RTT:
- t = 0: 2, 6: 4, 12: 8, 18: 16, 24: 32 (threshold reached)
- 30: 34, 36: 36, 42: 38, 48: 40, 54: 42, 60: 44

44 KB is still below the 50 KB receiver window.

Answer: 44
